findings.title: OptimizedImage.downsize is defined twice; the first definition is dead code and its callers break
findings.body: The file defines self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) at line 145 and then redefines self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={}) at line 149. In Ruby the second definition silently replaces the first, so the width/height variant can never be executed. Any existing caller still using the old signature breaks: a 5-argument call raises ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments), and a 4-argument call downsize(from, to, w, h) silently mis-binds so the integer height lands in opts, where optimize then calls opts[:allow_animation] on an Integer. Remove the leftover 145-147 definition and update any remaining callers instead of shipping two.

findings.title: Large animated GIFs are silently flattened to their first frame
findings.body: The new auto-downsize code calls OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: ...). OptimizedImage.optimize only selects the animated (gifsicle) instructions when `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`, but uploaded tempfiles (e.g. /tmp/RackMultipart...) have no extension, so the check never matches the original filename or the file content. Large animated GIFs therefore go through `convert <path>[0] ...`, which keeps only the first frame; the upload then succeeds with a static image and the user's animation is silently destroyed (previously the file was rejected for size and the user kept their original). The allow_animation option passed here is effectively dead for direct uploads; detect the format from the original filename or image content instead of the tempfile path.

findings.title: Client-side upload size check no longer honors max_image_size_kb / max_attachment_size_kb
findings.body: validateUploadedFile used to enforce Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']; it now hardcodes 10 MB for every upload type. Letting images up to 10 MB through is the point of this feature (the server downsizes them), but attachments are not downsized by the new server code (it only touches FileHelper.is_image? files), so: (a) an admin who set max_attachment_size_kb below 10 MB loses client-side enforcement and nothing in create_upload re-validates attachment size, and (b) an admin who set it above 10 MB has users wrongly rejected by the client. Additionally the 413 handler at line 246 now always reports a 10 MB maximum in the error message, which is wrong whenever the web server or site setting has a different limit. The 10 MB cap should apply to images; attachments should still be validated against their own setting.

findings.title: Downsize failures are ignored and the possibly-oversized original is uploaded anyway
findings.body: The while loop stops after 5 attempts regardless of whether tempfile.size is now within SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb, the boolean result of OptimizedImage.downsize is ignored, and nothing is logged when it returns false (e.g. when convert/gifsicle errors out). The possibly-still-oversized file then flows straight into Upload.create_for. A large image that resists reduction (very high resolution source, missing/broken ImageMagick) is therefore either silently stored far above the configured limit or fails later with an unrelated error. Check the size after the loop and log or reject when the attempts are exhausted.

findings.title: Animated downsize passes "80%" to gifsicle --resize-fit, which only accepts WxH geometry
findings.body: downsize_instructions_animated delegates to resize_instructions_animated, producing `gifsicle --resize-fit 80%`. gifsicle's --resize-fit requires explicit WIDTHxHEIGHT pixel dimensions and does not understand ImageMagick-style percentages, so any animated downsize through this path exits non-zero and convert_with returns false without resizing. Previously the animated path only ever received "WxH" strings; the new percentage-based flow needs its own animated instructions (e.g. gifsicle --scale 0.8) or computed pixel dimensions.

findings.title: Every 80% retry also runs the full ImageOptim pipeline on the intermediate file
findings.body: Each loop iteration calls OptimizedImage.downsize -> convert_with, which runs ImageOptim.new.optimize_image! (jpegoptim/pngcrush/etc.) on the intermediate result, only for the next iteration to overwrite it. Worst case that is five full optimization passes per upload where one final pass would suffice; for multi-megabyte PNGs this adds tens of seconds of CPU in the deferred job and can push the synchronous API upload path (is_api? && params[:synchronous]) toward request timeouts. Resize without optimizing inside the loop and optimize once at the end.

findings.title: No specs cover the new auto-downsize upload flow
findings.body: The PR changes upload size enforcement on both client and server, adds a resize loop in create_upload, and changes OptimizedImage.downsize's signature, but no spec files are touched. Controller/model specs that upload an image larger than max_image_size_kb would catch the regressions visible here (animated GIFs flattened to one frame, the duplicate downsize definition, the loop storing oversized originals when attempts run out). The feature currently ships untested.
